Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "I’m gathering concrete input for Owen’s 2028 performance discussion. Create one short evidence note based on the earlier first-pass packet reviews, identifying the relevant packet examples, which source-completeness fields were present, and how much hands-on structural correction I had to provide. Then email Priya Devarajan a concise summary with the same bounded conclusion.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Owen 2028 performance discussion — source-structure evidence note", "folder": "Team", "body": "Evidence note — Owen’s earlier first-pass packet reviews

Relevant examples: the July monthly sanitized campaign snapshot, the Q2 source lock, and the complete August Helio Start paid-pilot packet. Each first pass included the source-completeness structure needed for review: denominator or coverage dates, outcome window, measurement limits, exclusions, source owner, reliability evidence, and explicit revenue and forecast treatment. In the later four-lane packet review, Owen also checked unchanged definitions, named-owner certification, and cross-surface consistency while reconciling the engineering-decision and reliability sources through October 31.

Hands-on structural correction: none line-by-line was required for the July, Q2, or August first passes. My involvement was review of the evidence and its boundaries, not rebuilding the packet structure. When the October packet’s source coverage and owner certification did not share the same exact through-date, Owen kept it incomplete and continued the reconciliation rather than presenting it as closed; that was a demonstrated fail-closed source-completeness behavior, not a structural correction I supplied.

Bounded conclusion: the reviewed examples demonstrate reliable first-pass source organization, explicit completeness fields, reconciliation discipline, and appropriate handling of unresolved source conditions. They support a conclusion about demonstrated source-structure and routine source-completeness performance only.
